what_it_does: When an AI model is serving many users at once, its working memory — the running notes it keeps for each conversation, called a key-value cache — can overflow the video card's on-board memory. Existing systems either refuse new requests or pause (preempt) ongoing ones and shuffle those notes to slow system RAM, which hurts speed. Aqua instead uses the high-speed chip-to-chip links (NVLink/NVSwitch — cables inside a server that connect GPUs at very high bandwidth) to stash those paused notes in the memory of a neighboring GPU rather than in slow RAM. Because the link is much faster than going out to the host computer's memory, the pause is far shorter, letting the system handle bursty request waves without sacrificing throughput.
